title: The reality of launching an indie game on Steam. Here are my actual numbers.
author: PandaRojasStudios
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/7scu0c15581i1.png

  
I'm an indie developer working on Nova Survivors, a sci-fi roguelite bullet heaven game.

I wanted to share some real numbers from our Steam journey so far. No marketing projections, no inflated success stories, just actual results.

\- $269 gross revenue

\- $227 net revenue

\- 165 total units (including retail activations)

\- 287+ wishlists

\- 108 lifetime unique users

\- 3 hours median playtime

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4982990/Nova\_Survivors/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4982990/Nova_Survivors/)

Are these impressive numbers? Probably not. But every sale, wishlist, review, and player interaction means something when you're building a game as an indie developer.

We're still learning, improving the game, fixing bugs, balancing gameplay, and trying to build something people genuinely enjoy.

How did your first months on Steam go? What would you have done differently?

Always happy to exchange experiences and learn from other developers.
